q: Deoxyribonucleic acid is the master blueprint for life. (2025-Set 3)
e: DNA carries the primary genetic instructions required for the development, functioning, and reproduction of living organisms.

q: The study of chemical, physical structures, and functions of biological microorganisms is known as molecular biology. (2024-Set 4)
e: Molecular biology is the study of biological activity at the molecular level, focusing on interactions between DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis.

q: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid and ribonucleic acid. (2024-Set 3)
e: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA) are the two primary types of nucleic acids.

q: Nucleic acids are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Nucleic acids store, express, and transmit cellular genetic information.

q: Each polynucleotide strand is made up of few nucleotide molecules. (2025-Set 4)
e: Each polynucleotide strand is a long chain composed of many repeating nucleotide monomers.

q: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary base pair in RNA. (2025-Set 9)
e: RNA is typically single-stranded, whereas hydrogen bonds link complementary base pairs in double-stranded DNA.

q: Adenine (A) and thymine (T) are joined by three hydrogen bonds. (2025-Set 8)
e: Adenine and thymine are linked by two hydrogen bonds, while cytosine and guanine are linked by three.

q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are antiparallel. (2025-Set 2,13)
e: The two complementary strands of a DNA double helix run in opposite 5' to 3' directions.

q: The purine bases are cytosine and thymine. (2025-Set 12)
e: Cytosine and thymine are pyrimidines; adenine and guanine are the purine bases.

q: The two strands of a RNA molecule are antiparallel. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများစုတွင်မေး)
e: RNA molecules are generally single-stranded rather than two antiparallel strands.

q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are parallel. (2024-Set 3 / 2025-Set 1)
e: The strands of a DNA molecule run in opposite directions, making them antiparallel.

q: DNA molecules are oriented differently. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: DNA molecules maintain a uniform, standard double-helical structure with antiparallel orientation.

q: DNA replication is the making of an exact copy of the RNA molecule. (2026-Set 1)
e: DNA replication is the process of synthesizing an exact replica of an existing DNA molecule.

q: Topoisomerase enzyme unwinds the parental double helix at replication forks. (2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Helicase unwinds the double helix, while topoisomerase relieves strain ahead of the replication fork.

q: Helicase enzymes unwind the double helix and unzip the two parental strands by breaking hydrogen bonds. (2025-Set 11)
e: Helicase separates parental DNA strands by breaking the hydrogen bonds between base pairs.

q: DNA polymerase III can initiate the synthesis of new strands of new DNA strand. (2025-Set 5)
e: DNA polymerase III cannot start synthesis de novo; it requires an RNA primer.

q: DNA replication is the making of an exact copy of the DNA molecule. (2024-Set 2)
e: Replication produces two identical double-stranded DNA copies prior to cell division.

q: DNA polymerase replicates the two original strands differently. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများစုတွင်မေး / 2025-Set 1, 7 / 2026-Set 2)
e: The leading strand is synthesized continuously, while the lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously.

q: There are only three codons that do not code for any amino acid. (2025-Set 12)
e: The three stop codons (UAA, UAG, and UGA) signal translation termination rather than coding for amino acids.

q: In transcription, mRNA is synthesized based on the RNA template of a gene. (2025-Set 7)
e: mRNA is synthesized using a complementary DNA strand as a template.

q: In transcription, mRNA is synthesized based on the DNA template of a gene. (2025-Set 8)
e: During transcription, RNA polymerase uses a specific DNA template strand to build mRNA.

q: The translation of nucleotide sequence to amino acid sequence uses the genetic code. (2025-Set 9)
e: The genetic code correlates triplets of mRNA nucleotides to specific amino acids.

q: The termination phase begins when a stop codon on the tRNA is reached. (2026-Set 2)
e: Termination occurs when a stop codon on the mRNA strand reaches the ribosomal A site.

q: The second stage of protein synthesis involves translation which occurs in the nucleus. (2025-Set 13)
e: Translation occurs on ribosomes in the cytoplasm, whereas transcription occurs in the nucleus.

q: Vitamin A deficiency can cause blindness. (2025-Set 11)
e: Lack of vitamin A severely affects vision health and can lead to irreversible blindness.

q: Golden rice contains a lot of beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin B. (2025-Set 6)
e: Beta-carotene is converted by the body into vitamin A, not vitamin B.

q: The beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin C when it is eaten. (2025-Set 10)
e: Ingested beta-carotene is converted into vitamin A.

q: Plants are also being engineered to produce medicinal products. (2025-Set 5)
e: Transgenic plants are used to produce therapeutic proteins, vaccines, and antibodies.

q: One type of antibody made by corn can deliver radioisotopes to tumour cells. (2025-Set 6 / 2026- Set 1)
e: Genetically modified corn can produce antibodies that specifically target tumor cells to deliver treatment.

q: The genetically modified rice is called Golden Rice. (2024-Set 4, နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Rice modified to biosynthesize beta-carotene is named Golden Rice.

q: Golden Rice contains a lot of the orange pigment beta-carotene. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Golden Rice is enriched with beta-carotene, giving its grains an orange-yellow hue.
